title: Native TEXT ASCII classification for the row decoder
impact: `decodeQuery` cannot build a Dart `String` from a TEXT cell until it knows whether the payload is pure ASCII (`String.fromCharCodes` widen) or not (`utf8.decode`), and it was answering that itself: a second `ExternalTypedData` word view plus a bounds-checked scan per cell, degrading to a byte-by-byte loop for anything under 16 bytes — which is most database text. `resqlite_step_row` already holds the pointer and length one frame earlier, where the same question is a branch-free SWAR pass over bytes still in cache. Moved it there: `text_is_ascii` reports `RESQLITE_TEXT_ASCII` (type code 6, the first value SQLite's 1-5 leaves free) and the decoder's TEXT arm splits into a widen path and a straight-to-`utf8.decode` path with no scan of its own. The stream hash is untouched — `resqlite_step_row_hash` folds the local `SQLITE_TEXT` before the switch, so the canonical digest still matches `resqlite_query_hash` (the exp 228 invariant). Focused AOT A/B, two order-flipped passes, `ab_drift_check` REPRODUCED on every primary lane: 10k x 8 short ASCII TEXT -12.3% / -10.4%, 40 B -14.3% / -10.7%, 2k x 4 400 B -22.2% / -19.4%, and the default 6-column mixed product row -7.8% / -7.8%. The two neutral lanes carry the verdict: the INTEGER-only control runs byte-identical code in both arms and moves +0.2% / -2.9% (opposite signs, inside the 3% floor), ruling out the exp 254 per-worktree binary offset; and the CJK guard is -2.4% / -1.7%, confirming that scanning a non-ASCII value to the end in C costs less than the partial Dart scan it replaced. A `resqlite_test_text_is_ascii` differential test plus an every-offset multibyte `select()` round trip gate the classification, since a wrong answer is silent mojibake rather than a crash.
